pride_data.title: Utilization of high-resolution mass spectrometry and data-independent analysis to track the monoclonal antibody spatial stability
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled with mass spectrometry (CXMS) offers the distance constraints critical for building the structural model of protein and protein complexes and understanding dynamics of biological systems. Originally developed for protein structural models, CXMS has evolved into method for studying protein complex formation, ligand-induced conformational changes, and quantitative structural analysis using isotopically labeled cross-linkers. In this study we tested the potential of isotopically labelled MS-cleavable cross-linker to track the stability of the therapeutic monoclonal antibodies. A novel isotopically labelled MS-cleavable cross-linker was synthesized, and its reactivity was successfully tested on peptide and protein standards. Further, the novel cross-linker was utilized to test the stability of selected therapeutical monoclonal antibodies, Avastin and Herceptin, adopting the data-independent acquisition. This study reports the advantages of using combination of 13C isotopically labelled MS-cleavable cross-linkers and data-independent mass spectrometry analysis for the automated identification of cross-linked products and thus monitoring the structural rearrangement of protein structure.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Every chemical cross-linking experiment was carried out in a cross-linking buffer (15 mM HEPES, 50 mM NaCl, pH 7.5). The cross-linking reactions were incubated at room temperature for 30 minutes. Both cross-linkers were freshly prepared before the reaction by dissolution in anhydrous DMSO. Oxidized beta chain of insulin (95 μM) was cross-linked using five molar excesses of a DSPU/DSPUx mixture in a 1:1 ratio. Human carbonic anhydrase (HCA) and bovine serum albumin (BSA), both (20 μM) was cross-linked (50 mol. eq.) with a mixture of DSPU/DSPUx in 9:1, 1:1 and 1:9 ratios (each ratio in a triplicate to ensure reproducibility). To monitor the stability of bevacizumab and trastuzumab, the following approach was utilized: 100 μg of each antibody diluted in the cross-linking buffer was cross-linked using 100 molar excess of DSPU or its isotopically labelled analog DSPUx (samples A). To induce structural changes in the antibodies’ structure, 50 μg of each antibody diluted in the cross-linking buffer was incubated at 4, 25 or 40 °C for 72 hours. Afterwards, the volume of every sample was divided into halves. One half of each sample was cross-linked with DSPU and the other half with DSPUx (samples B). To determine the changes of the antibodies’ structure, the samples B were mixed in a 1:1 ratio with samples A in both combinations, that is light type cross-link sample A combined with heavy type cross-link sample B and heavy type cross-link sample A with light type cross-link sample B. Non cross-linked antibodies and antibodies cross-linked in a 1:1 ratio of DSPU/DSPUx were used as control samples. The quantitative cross-linking of the apo/holomyoglobin model system (39 μM) was performed in the following way: Apomyoglobin and holomyoglobin were each cross-linked (100 mol. eq.) with DSPU (light type cross-link) or its isotopically labeled analog DSPUx (heavy type cross-link). Afterwards, the different myoglobin forms were combined in a 1:1 ratio so that the cross-linked apo-form was combined with the isotopically cross-linked holo-form and vice versa. To ensure reproducibility, all the samples were prepared in a triplicate. Apomyoglobin, holomyoglobin, apomyoglobin cross-linked with a DSPU/DSPUx mixture in a 1:1 ratio and holomyoglobin cross-linked with a DSPU/DSPUx mixture in a 1:1 ratio were used as control samples. Reaction mixtures were six times diluted with 0.1% TFA and desalted using the MicroTrap (Optimize Technologies, USA). Elution was performed using a solution of 80% ACN, 0.1% TFA. The eluted volume was 50 μl. The desalted samples were further 25 times diluted with a spraying solution (50% methanol, 0.1% formic acid) and sprayed into the 15T solariX XR mass spectrometer (Bruker Daltonics). The instrument was operated in a positive mode with 1M transient data points and m/z range of 250-2500. After the cross-linking reaction, the samples were diluted (one time) with a 100 mM 4 ethylmorpholine buffer (pH 8.5). Protein hydrolysis was performed using the trypsin protease (protein:enzyme ratio 20:1). The proteolysis was performed overnight at 37 °C. In case of HCA, BSA and antibodies that contained disulfide bridges, tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (final concentration 5 mM) and 2-chloroacetamide (final concentration 10 mM) were added to the diluted sample and kept for five minutes at 70 °C. The digestion was stopped by the addition of TFA to a final concentration of 0.1% and the resulting peptide mixture was dried using SpeedVac (Eppendorf, Germany). In case of the antibodies, after the reduction and alkylation of cysteines, urea (final concentration 1M) and thiourea (final concentration 1M) were added to the samples. Afterwards, samples were heated to 37 °C and LysC protease (protein:enzyme ratio 20:1) was utilized. After four hours of LysC proteolysis, trypsin was added (protein:enzyme ratio 20:1) to the mixture. The digestion was performed overnight and stopped by the addition of TFA to a final concentration of 0.1%. The samples were processed as described previously22. Briefly, samples were reconstituted with 30 μl of 0.1% FA and five μl was injected using the Agilent 1290 series UPLC system onto a desalting precolumn Luna Omega Polar C18 (5 μm, 100 Å, 0.3 × 30 mm) at a flow rate of 20 μl/min. After five minutes, the peptides were separated using an analytical column Luna Omega Polar C18 (3 μm, 100 Å, 0.3 × 150 mm) heated to 50 °C at a flow rate of 10 μl/min. The acetonitrile gradient of 5% to 35% over 35 minutes was used. The chromatographic system was connected to an electrospray source of the solariX XR (Bruker Daltonics) mass spectrometer equipped with a 15T superconducting magnet.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: The data obtained using the bottom-up approach were deconvoluted using the SNAP 2.0 algorithm and exported to a .mgf file in the DataAnalysis 4.4 software using self-written script. specifically, the script dissects chromatogram into scans where each individual mass spectrum corresponds to one scan. Even-numbered mass spectra correspond to MS traces whereas odd-numbered spectra to MS/MS trace. All assigned m/z value from MS spectra together with intensity value are exported to txt file that can serve as input for LinX software. All assigned m/z value from each MS/MS spectra together with intensity value are exported to peak list into mgf file which adheres standard mgf file format.The exported data were further analyzed using the LinX software 1.12 and MeroX 2.0.1.423,24.  LinX software was used with the following parameters: MS1 precision 1 ppm, cleavage after: lysine and arginine, number of miscleavages: 3 and methionine oxidation as a variable modification. In case of protein samples that contained disulfide bridges, carbamidomethylation was set as a fixed modification. N-terminus and lysine were considered as targets of cross-linking reaction. MeroX software was used with the following parameters: MS1 precision: 1.0 ppm, MS2 precision 2.0 ppm, cleavage after: lysine and arginine, number of miscleavages: 3, variable modifications: oxidation of methionine, static modifications: carbamidomethylation of cysteine in case carbamidomethylation was utilized in sample preparation, cross-linker specificity sites: lysine, serine, threonine, tyrosine, N-terminus.  The ratio of modification with DSPU was calculated from fragments using the following equation: (Intensity DSPU) / ((Intensity DSPU) + Intensity (DSPUx)), where (Intensity DSPU) is the intensity of the highest intensity peak of the isotopic distribution of the identified fragment of light cross-link and (Intensity DSPUx) is the intensity of the corresponding isotopic peak of the heavy fragment of cross-link.
